reasons: Deviation call is supported: p0016 bars any Customer convenience exit during the Initial Term, gives Kubient a symmetric 'for any reason' exit that operates mid-renewal-term on 90 days' notice, provides no pro-rata refund, and entitles Kubient to all fees generated during the termination period (an effective early-termination penalty) — all short of the preferred position.

Redline reaches the preferred position with directionally correct, customer-favourable changes: a 30-day Customer convenience right (expressly including the Initial Term), refund of prepaid fees, no early-termination penalty, Kubient's convenience right confined to effect at the end of the then-current Term on 90 days' notice, and the fee entitlement trimmed to fees through the effective date.

Deletion of the 'Neither Party may terminate during the Initial Term' sentence is necessary because it directly contradicts the new Customer right, and Kubient's restriction is expressly re-stated, so no counterparty right is inadvertently expanded; breach/insolvency rights in 4(b) are untouched.

Failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.695 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here — the rule requires restructuring the reciprocal convenience/fee sentences, and the edit is confined to those sentences.
Comment is accurate, correctly states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the 60-day / vendor 90-day end-of-term fallback in the required tone and prefix.
